name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
description: The single-arm kettlebell swing applies the hip hinge mechanics of the two-handed swing to one arm, which introduces an anti-rotation challenge for the core and demands greater grip strength. The free arm can be used as a counterbalance or held at the side. Training one arm at a time addresses left-right imbalances and builds rotational core stability that bilateral swings cannot replicate.

execution.starting_position: Stand with feet hip-width, kettlebell between feet. Hinge at the hips and grasp the handle with one hand.
execution.setup_instructions: Master two-handed swings before moving to single-arm. Use the same weight or slightly less than your two-handed swing.
steps: Step 1: Hike the kettlebell back between the legs as in a standard swing.
Step 2: Drive the hips forward explosively, swinging the kettlebell to shoulder height.
Step 3: Keep the free arm swinging naturally as a counterbalance — it can swing opposite the kettlebell.
Step 4: Control the bell back between the legs and repeat for reps, then switch sides.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale sharply at the hip snap, inhale on the downswing.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso toward the working arm
Letting the shoulder shrug upward at the top
safety_considerations: Keep the spine neutral — resist torso rotation
Build up gradually — the unilateral demand is high
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Hip hinge to full hip extension with bell at shoulder height.
coaching_cues: Hips drive the bell — not the arm
